attributes.description: Foreign key linking to partnership.partner_org. Business justification: In consortium and area-based approaches, partners are assigned responsibility for specific communities or geographic zones. Tracking the lead partner per community enables coordination, avoids duplica

attributes.name: staff_member_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the staff member or enumerator who registered the community in the system. Used for data quality accountability and field operations management.

attributes.name: access_constraint_level
attributes.description: Level of operational access constraints affecting the community due to security incidents, administrative restrictions, natural barriers, or conflict dynamics. No constraint: full access. Low: minor delays. Medium: significant restrictions. High: severely constrained. No access: inaccessible. Used for operational planning and risk management.

attributes.name: active_program_count
attributes.description: Number of active humanitarian or development programs currently operating in the community. Used for coordination, gap analysis, and 3W (Who does What Where) reporting.

attributes.name: admin1_code
attributes.description: First-level administrative division code (province, state, governorate) where the community is located. Aligns with OCHA Common Operational Dataset Administrative Boundaries (COD-AB) P-codes for standardized geographic reporting.
attributes.references: OCHA COD-AB (Common Operational Dataset - Administrative Boundaries) Standards

attributes.name: admin1_name
attributes.description: Name of the first-level administrative division (province, state, governorate) where the community is located. Human-readable complement to admin1_code.

attributes.name: admin2_code
attributes.description: Second-level administrative division code (district, county, department) where the community is located. Aligns with OCHA COD-AB P-codes for standardized geographic reporting.

attributes.name: admin2_name
attributes.description: Name of the second-level administrative division (district, county, department) where the community is located. Human-readable complement to admin2_code.

attributes.name: admin3_code
attributes.description: Third-level administrative division code (sub-district, municipality) where the community is located. Aligns with OCHA COD-AB P-codes where available.

attributes.name: admin3_name
attributes.description: Name of the third-level administrative division (sub-district, municipality) where the community is located. Human-readable complement to admin3_code.

attributes.name: admin4_code
attributes.description: Fourth-level administrative division code (village, neighborhood, locality) where the community is located. Aligns with OCHA COD-AB P-codes where available.

attributes.name: admin4_name
attributes.description: Name of the fourth-level administrative division (village, neighborhood, locality) where the community is located. Human-readable complement to admin4_code.

attributes.name: community_code
attributes.description: Externally-known unique business identifier or code for the community, used in field operations, 3W (Who does What Where) reporting, and inter-agency coordination. May align with OCHA P-codes or agency-specific community identifiers.
attributes.references: OCHA Common Operational Dataset (COD) Standards, IATI Activity Identifier Standards

attributes.name: community_name
attributes.description: Official or commonly-used name of the community, settlement, camp, or geographic area. This is the primary human-readable identifier used in field reports, SitReps (Situation Reports), and beneficiary communications.

attributes.name: community_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the community registration. Active: community is currently served by programs. Inactive: temporarily not served. Closed: community no longer exists or is no longer a target. Planned: community identified for future programming. Suspended: operations temporarily halted due to access constraints or security incidents.

attributes.name: consent_date
attributes.description: Date when community consent was obtained for data collection and program activities. Used for consent tracking and compliance documentation.

attributes.name: consent_obtained_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether informed consent was obtained from community leadership or representatives for data collection, program implementation, and data sharing. True if consent obtained, False otherwise. Supports CHS (Core Humanitarian Standard) accountability commitments and GDPR compliance where applicable.
attributes.references: CHS Commitment 4 - Community Participation, GDPR Article 6

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code where the community is located. Used for country-level aggregation, compliance reporting, and IATI (International Aid Transparency Initiative) transparency reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 Country Codes, IATI Country Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this community record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: data_sharing_consent_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the community has consented to sharing of community-level data with partner organizations, clusters, or coordination bodies. True if data sharing permitted, False otherwise. Supports inter-agency coordination while respecting community preferences.
attributes.references: IASC Operational Data Sharing Protocols, GDPR Article 6

attributes.name: displacement_status
attributes.description: Classification of the community based on displacement dynamics. Host community: existing community hosting displaced populations. IDP settlement: community primarily composed of Internally Displaced Persons. Refugee camp: formal refugee settlement. Returnee community: community of returned displaced persons. Mixed: combination of host and displaced populations.

attributes.name: estimated_population
attributes.description: Estimated total number of individuals residing in or associated with the community. This is the principal quantitative measurement for the community resource, used for needs calculations, resource allocation, and coverage reporting.
attributes.references: OCHA Common Operational Dataset (COD) Population Statistics Standards

attributes.name: gbv_risk_level
attributes.description: Assessment of GBV risk level in the community based on safety audits, incident reports, and vulnerability indicators. Used for GBV prevention programming, safe space establishment, and referral pathway planning.
attributes.references: IASC GBV Guidelines, UNFPA GBV Information Management System Standards

attributes.name: gps_accuracy_meters
attributes.business_glossary_term: GPS (Global Positioning System) Accuracy in Meters
attributes.description: Accuracy of the GPS coordinates in meters. Indicates the precision of the latitude and longitude measurements, important for field data quality assessment and spatial analysis reliability.

attributes.name: health_facility_distance_km
attributes.description: Distance in kilometers from the community to the nearest functional health facility. Used for health access analysis, referral planning, and mobile health outreach prioritization.
attributes.references: Sphere Humanitarian Standards - Health Systems Minimum Standards

attributes.name: household_count
attributes.description: Estimated or verified number of households within the community. Used for household-level targeting and distribution planning in WASH, shelter, and NFI (Non-Food Item) programs.

attributes.name: ipc_phase
attributes.business_glossary_term: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) Phase
attributes.description: IPC acute food insecurity phase classification for the community. Phase 1: Minimal/None. Phase 2: Stressed. Phase 3: Crisis. Phase 4: Emergency. Phase 5: Catastrophe/Famine. Used for food security targeting and early warning.
attributes.references: IPC (Integrated Food Security Phase Classification) Global Standards

attributes.name: last_assessment_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent needs assessment or monitoring visit conducted in the community. Used to track data currency and schedule follow-up assessments.

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate (decimal degrees) of the community centroid or primary access point. Used for GIS (Geographic Information System) mapping, spatial analysis, and proximity-based service planning.
attributes.references: WGS84 Geographic Coordinate System, OCHA COD-AB Standards

attributes.name: leader_contact
attributes.description: Primary contact information (phone number or other communication channel) for the community leader or representative. Used for coordination, consultation, and feedback mechanisms. Classified as confidential PII.
attributes.references: CHS Commitment 5 - Complaints Mechanism, GDPR Article 4

attributes.name: leader_name
attributes.description: Name of the primary community leader, elder, or representative. Used for community engagement, consultation, and accountability mechanisms. Classified as confidential to protect community leadership in sensitive contexts.
attributes.references: CHS (Core Humanitarian Standard) Commitment 4 - Community Participation

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate (decimal degrees) of the community centroid or primary access point. Used for GIS mapping, spatial analysis, and proximity-based service planning.
attributes.references: WGS84 Geographic Coordinate System, OCHA COD-AB Standards

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this community record was last modified. Used for audit trail, change tracking, and data currency assessment.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional contextual information, operational notes, or special considerations about the community. Used for qualitative context that does not fit structured fields.

attributes.name: primary_language_code
attributes.description: ISO 639-3 three-letter code for the primary language spoken in the community. Used for communication planning, translation needs, and culturally appropriate programming.

attributes.name: protection_concern_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the community has been flagged for protection concerns such as GBV (Gender-Based Violence) risk, child protection issues, or other safety and security threats. True if protection concerns exist, False otherwise. Used for protection mainstreaming and specialized protection interventions.

attributes.name: registration_date
attributes.description: Date when the community was first registered in the system as a collective beneficiary unit for area-based programming. This is the principal business event timestamp for the community entity.

attributes.name: registration_source
attributes.description: Source system or tool used to register the community (e.g., KoboToolbox, CommCare, DHIS2, manual field assessment). Used for data lineage tracking and quality assessment.

attributes.name: sanitation_coverage_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of households in the community with access to adequate sanitation facilities (latrines, toilets) meeting Sphere minimum standards (1 toilet per 20 people). Used for WASH gap analysis and intervention planning.
attributes.references: Sphere Humanitarian Standards - WASH Minimum Standards

attributes.name: settlement_type
attributes.description: Classification of the community or settlement type. Formal camp: officially designated refugee or IDP (Internally Displaced Person) camp. Informal settlement: spontaneous or unplanned settlement. Host community: existing community hosting displaced populations. Collective center: shared facility (school, warehouse) used for temporary shelter. Transit site: temporary waypoint for displaced populations. Urban area: city or town neighborhood.
attributes.references: UNHCR Settlement Classification Standards, Sphere Humanitarian Standards

attributes.name: vulnerability_category
attributes.description: Categorical classification of community vulnerability level derived from vulnerability_score. Critical: immediate life-saving assistance required. High: urgent multi-sectoral needs. Medium: moderate needs requiring monitoring. Low: stable with minimal humanitarian needs. Used for targeting and resource allocation decisions.

attributes.name: vulnerability_score
attributes.description: Composite vulnerability score for the community based on multi-sectoral needs assessment indicators (WASH, shelter, food security, protection, health). Higher scores indicate greater vulnerability and higher priority for humanitarian assistance. Scoring methodology aligns with agency-specific vulnerability assessment frameworks.
attributes.references: IASC (Inter-Agency Standing Committee) Humanitarian Needs Overview Standards

attributes.name: water_access_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the community has adequate access to safe water sources according to Sphere minimum standards (15 liters per person per day within 500 meters). True if adequate access exists, False otherwise. Used for WASH (Water Sanitation and Hygiene) needs prioritization.
attributes.references: Sphere Humanitarian Standards - WASH Minimum Standards

attributes.name: parent_community_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on community (parent_community_id)

products.name: service_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the operational assignment of volunteers to beneficiaries for service delivery in community-based programming. It captures the service relationship between a volunteer and a registrant, including service type, duration, frequency, and delivery status. Each record links one volunteer to one beneficiary they are actively serving or have served, with attributes that exist only in the context of this service delivery relationship. This is the operational record that case managers and program coordinators use to track volunteer caseloads and beneficiary service coverage.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit community-based programming, volunteers serve multiple beneficiaries simultaneously as part of their caseload (a community health worker serves 20-30 households, a PSS counselor supports 15-20 individuals), and beneficiaries receive services from multiple volunteers over time and across service types (one beneficiary may have a nutrition monitor, a case manager, and a community health worker). Program coordinators actively manage these service assignments, tracking who serves whom, with what service type, at what frequency, and with what status.

attributes.name: service_assignment_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for each volunteer-beneficiary service assignment record. Primary key for the association.

attributes.name: registrant_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the beneficiary registrant receiving services from the volunteer

attributes.name: staff_member_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the program coordinator or case manager who made this volunteer-beneficiary assignment.

attributes.name: volunteer_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the volunteer providing services to the beneficiary

attributes.name: assignment_date
attributes.description: The date when this volunteer was formally assigned to this beneficiary by program coordination staff.

attributes.name: case_load_priority
attributes.description: Priority level of this beneficiary within the volunteer's caseload. Explicitly identified in detection reasoning as relationship data.

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: The date when the volunteer stopped or is scheduled to stop providing services to this beneficiary. Null indicates ongoing service. Explicitly identified in detection reasoning as relationship data.

attributes.name: frequency
attributes.description: How frequently the volunteer provides services to this beneficiary. Explicitly identified in detection reasoning as relationship data.

attributes.name: location
attributes.description: The location where services are delivered (community center, home visit, health post, etc.). Explicitly identified in detection reasoning as relationship data.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes about this specific service assignment, including special considerations, beneficiary preferences, or coordination details.

attributes.name: service_delivery_status
attributes.description: Current status of the service delivery relationship between this volunteer and beneficiary. Explicitly identified in detection reasoning as relationship data.

attributes.name: service_type
attributes.description: The type of service the volunteer is providing to this beneficiary. Explicitly identified in detection reasoning as relationship data.

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: The date when the volunteer began providing services to this beneficiary. Explicitly identified in detection reasoning as relationship data.

attributes.name: supervision_level
attributes.description: The level of supervision required for this volunteer-beneficiary service relationship. Explicitly identified in detection reasoning as relationship data.

products.name: household_volunteer_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the assignment relationship between households and volunteers in community-based service delivery programs. It captures the operational assignment of volunteers to specific households for ongoing service delivery, visit tracking, and workload management. Each record links one household to one volunteer with attributes that track assignment lifecycle, visit schedules, and service delivery context.. Existence Justification: In community-based humanitarian service delivery, volunteers are operationally assigned to multiple households within their geographic catchment area (a community health worker may serve 20-30 households), and households receive services from multiple volunteers over time across different program areas (health, nutrition, protection, livelihoods). The assignment relationship is actively managed by program coordinators who create assignments, track visit schedules, monitor service delivery, and reassign households based on volunteer availability and workload balancing.

attributes.name: household_volunteer_assignment_id
attributes.description: Primary key for household_volunteer_assignment

attributes.name: assignment_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for the household-volunteer assignment record. Primary key.

attributes.name: household_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the household receiving volunteer services

attributes.name: volunteer_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the volunteer assigned to provide services

attributes.name: assignment_date
attributes.description: Calendar date when the volunteer was formally assigned to this household for service delivery. Marks the beginning of the assignment relationship.

attributes.name: assignment_end_date
attributes.description: Calendar date when the assignment was formally ended or closed. Null for active assignments. Used for historical tracking and volunteer engagement reporting.

attributes.name: assignment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the volunteer-household assignment. Active indicates ongoing service delivery, Suspended indicates temporary pause, Completed indicates assignment ended successfully, Transferred indicates household reassigned to another volunteer.

attributes.name: assignment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the service delivery type for this assignment. Defines the primary program area or service category the volunteer provides to the household.

attributes.name: geographic_area
attributes.description: Geographic zone, sector, or catchment area identifier for this assignment. Used to group households by volunteer service area for workload balancing and geographic coverage planning.

attributes.name: last_visit_date
attributes.description: Calendar date of the most recent visit by this volunteer to this household. Updated after each completed visit for monitoring and follow-up scheduling.

attributes.name: next_visit_date
attributes.description: Calendar date of the next scheduled visit by this volunteer to this household. Used for volunteer scheduling and workload planning.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for capturing assignment-specific notes, special instructions, household preferences, or contextual information relevant to service delivery.

attributes.name: visit_frequency
attributes.description: Expected frequency of volunteer visits to the household based on program requirements and household needs assessment.

products.name: community_intervention
products.description: This association product represents the implementation relationship between a community and an intervention. It captures the operational deployment of a humanitarian or development intervention to a specific community, including implementation timeline, household targeting and reach metrics, coverage status, and geographic implementation type. Each record links one community to one intervention with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific implementation deployment.. Existence Justification: In humanitarian operations, one intervention is routinely deployed across multiple communities (multi-site implementation is standard for area-based programming), and one community simultaneously receives multiple interventions from different sectors (integrated programming is a core humanitarian principle - e.g., a refugee camp receives WASH, health, nutrition, and education interventions concurrently). NGOs actively manage these implementation relationships as operational entities, tracking start/end dates, household targeting vs. reach, and coverage status for each community-intervention pairing to support geographic reporting, cluster coordination (3W reporting), and community-level program monitoring required by humanitarian coordination mechanisms.

attributes.name: community_intervention_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this specific community-intervention implementation record

attributes.name: community_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the community where this intervention is being implemented

attributes.name: intervention_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the intervention being implemented in this community

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: Date when intervention activities concluded or are planned to conclude in this specific community. Explicitly identified in detection phase as relationship data.

attributes.name: geographic_coverage_type
attributes.description: Classification of how the intervention covers this community. Explicitly identified in detection phase as relationship data. Full community: all households eligible; Partial - targeted households: specific vulnerability-based targeting; Partial - geographic zone: specific neighborhoods/sectors; Pilot: test implementation.

attributes.name: implementation_status
attributes.description: Current status of intervention implementation in this specific community. Explicitly identified in detection phase as relationship data. Values: Planned (not yet started), Active (ongoing), Suspended (temporarily halted), Completed (activities finished), Closed (administratively closed).

attributes.name: reached_household_count
attributes.description: Actual number of households reached by this intervention in this specific community. Explicitly identified in detection phase as relationship data. Used for coverage calculation and donor reporting.

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: Date when intervention activities commenced in this specific community. Explicitly identified in detection phase as relationship data.

attributes.name: target_household_count
attributes.description: Number of households this intervention aims to reach in this specific community. Explicitly identified in detection phase as relationship data.

products.name: enrollment
products.description: This association product represents the enrollment relationship between a registrant and a program component. It captures the operational record of a beneficiary's participation in a specific component of a program intervention, including enrollment lifecycle, service delivery tracking, and component-specific outcome data required for donor reporting and MEL frameworks. Each record links one registrant to one component with attributes that exist only in the context of this enrollment relationship.. Existence Justification: In NGO operations, a single beneficiary registrant participates in multiple program components simultaneously or over time (e.g., a child receives nutrition screening, education support, and WASH services as separate component enrollments). Conversely, each program component serves multiple registrants. The enrollment relationship is actively managed by program staff who track enrollment dates, participation status, attendance, service delivery modality, and exit reasons for each registrant-component pairing. This enrollment data is essential for component-level reach reporting, disaggregated MEL indicators, and donor logframe reporting.

attributes.name: enrollment_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this enrollment record. Primary key for the enrollment association.

attributes.name: component_id
attributes.description: Foreign key to program.component. Identifies the program component in which the beneficiary is enrolled.

attributes.name: registrant_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the beneficiary registrant participating in this component enrollment

attributes.name: staff_member_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the NGO staff member or partner organization staff who processed this enrollment. Used for accountability, quality assurance, and workload tracking.

attributes.name: attendance_rate
attributes.description: Percentage of scheduled component activities or sessions that the registrant attended. Calculated as (sessions_attended / sessions_scheduled) * 100. Used for engagement monitoring, outcome correlation analysis, and donor reporting on program participation quality. Explicitly identified in detection phase.

attributes.name: completion_date
attributes.description: The date on which the registrant completed or exited this component enrollment. Null for active enrollments. Used for outcome tracking, retention analysis, and donor reporting on program completion rates. Explicitly identified in detection phase.

attributes.name: consent_for_component
attributes.description: Indicates whether the registrant (or guardian) provided informed consent specifically for participation in this component. Some components (e.g., health screening, psychosocial support) require additional consent beyond general registration consent.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.description: System timestamp when this enrollment record was created in the database. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: enrollment_date
attributes.description: The date on which the registrant was formally enrolled into this program component. Used for cohort analysis, eligibility determination, and donor reporting on enrollment timelines. Explicitly identified in detection phase as enrollment_date.

attributes.name: enrollment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this enrollment record. Controls eligibility for component-specific services and activities. Values: enrolled (registered but not yet active), active (currently participating), suspended (temporarily paused), completed (successfully finished component), withdrawn (voluntarily left), exited (administratively removed). Explicitly identified in detection phase as enrollment_status.

attributes.name: exit_reason
attributes.description: Classification of the reason for enrollment termination or exit. Used for attrition analysis, program improvement, and donor reporting on retention and completion. Values include: completed (successfully finished), relocated (moved out of service area), deceased, ineligible (no longer meets criteria), voluntary-withdrawal, lost-to-follow-up, program-closure, other. Null for active enrollments. Explicitly identified in detection phase.

attributes.name: location
attributes.description: Geographic location (site, camp, community, district) where this enrollment was processed. Used for geographic disaggregation in MEL reporting and operational planning.

attributes.name: referral_source
attributes.description: Source of referral into this component enrollment (self-referral, community health worker, partner organization, internal program referral, vulnerability assessment). Used for referral pathway analysis and partnership coordination.

attributes.name: service_delivery_modality
attributes.description: The method or channel through which this component's services are delivered to the registrant. Distinguishes in-person group sessions, mobile outreach, remote/digital delivery, hybrid approaches, cash transfers, vouchers, or direct provision of goods/services. Critical for modality-disaggregated MEL reporting required by donors. Explicitly identified in detection phase.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.description: System timestamp when this enrollment record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

products.name: entitlement
products.description: This association product represents the entitlement relationship between registrant and commodity. It captures the humanitarian assistance entitlement rules that define which commodities each beneficiary is entitled to receive, in what quantities, at what frequency, and for what duration. Each record links one registrant to one commodity with entitlement-specific parameters including quantity per distribution cycle, distribution frequency, entitlement validity period, vulnerability-based adjustments, and special dietary requirements. This is the operational SSOT for ration planning, distribution planning, and beneficiary entitlement verification in food security and NFI distribution programs.. Existence Justification: In humanitarian operations, beneficiaries are entitled to receive multiple commodities simultaneously as part of their assistance package (e.g., a monthly food basket includes rice, oil, beans, salt, and a household receives multiple NFI items like blankets, jerry cans, soap). Each commodity is entitled to thousands of beneficiaries across the program. The entitlement relationship is an operational business entity actively managed by program officers, carrying specific data about quantity per distribution cycle, frequency, validity period, vulnerability-based adjustments, and special dietary requirements that belong to neither the beneficiary nor the commodity alone.

attributes.name: entitlement_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each beneficiary-commodity entitlement record

attributes.name: commodity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the humanitarian commodity that the beneficiary is entitled to receive

attributes.name: constituent_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the donor funding this specific entitlement, if donor-restricted commodities are involved. Used for donor reporting and compliance with donor-imposed restrictions on commodity use.

attributes.name: intervention_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the humanitarian program or intervention under which this entitlement is granted (e.g., General Food Distribution, Blanket Supplementary Feeding, Emergency NFI Distribution). Links entitlement to funding source and program reporting.

attributes.name: last_modified_by_user_user_account_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the system user who most recently modified this entitlement record. Used for accountability and audit purposes.

attributes.name: registrant_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the beneficiary registrant who holds this commodity entitlement

attributes.name: user_account_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the system user or program officer who created this entitlement record. Used for accountability and audit purposes.

attributes.name: created_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this entitlement record was created in the system. Used for audit trail and entitlement history tracking.

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: The date on which this entitlement expires or is scheduled to end. Null indicates ongoing entitlement subject to program continuation. Used for entitlement lifecycle management and program phase-out planning.

attributes.name: entitlement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this entitlement record. Controls whether the beneficiary is currently eligible to receive this commodity in distribution operations.

attributes.name: frequency
attributes.description: The frequency at which the beneficiary is entitled to receive this commodity (e.g., monthly food ration, one-time NFI kit, weekly fresh food distribution). Drives distribution cycle planning.

attributes.name: last_modified_date
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this entitlement record. Used for change tracking and synchronization.

attributes.name: quantity
attributes.description: The quantity of the commodity that the beneficiary is entitled to receive per distribution cycle, expressed in the commodity's standard unit of measure. Used for ration calculation and distribution planning.

attributes.name: special_dietary_requirement
attributes.description: Free-text description of any special dietary requirements, restrictions, or substitutions applicable to this beneficiary-commodity entitlement (e.g., halal, kosher, allergen-free, therapeutic food for MAM/SAM cases). Used for commodity substitution and specialized ration planning.

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: The date from which this entitlement becomes active and the beneficiary is eligible to receive the commodity. Used for entitlement verification and distribution eligibility checks.

attributes.name: vulnerability_based_adjustment
attributes.description: Multiplier or adjustment factor applied to the base entitlement quantity based on the beneficiary's vulnerability category, protection status, or special needs (e.g., 1.5x for pregnant/lactating women, 2.0x for severely malnourished children). Applied during ration calculation.

domains.name: program
domains.description: Owns the design, planning, and lifecycle management of all humanitarian and development interventions including WASH, health, nutrition, education, protection, and livelihood programs. Captures Theory of Change (ToC), LogFrame, SDG alignment, sector classifications, RBM (Results-Based Management) frameworks, and program hierarchies from proposal through closeout.

products.name: intervention
products.description: Core master entity representing a humanitarian or development program/intervention (e.g., WASH, health, nutrition, education, protection, livelihoods). Captures the full program lifecycle from design through closeout, including program type (emergency vs. development), phase, status, start/end dates, geographic scope, target population summary, organizational ownership, and SDG alignment mappings (goal, target, indicator, alignment type, contribution narrative). This is the primary anchor entity for the program domain and the SSOT for all program-level identity, metadata, design narrative (situation analysis, intervention logic, targeting strategy, sustainability plan), and strategic framework alignment. All other program domain entities reference this as their parent.
products.reference: OCHA Humanitarian Programme Cycle (HPC); IATI Activity Standard

attributes.name: intervention_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the humanitarian or development intervention/program. Primary key for the intervention entity.

attributes.name: compliance_obligation_id

attributes.name: finance_fund_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.finance_fund. Business justification: Programs are funded by specific restricted or unrestricted funds. Essential for donor compliance reporting, financial tracking, and ensuring expenditures align with fund restrictions. Nonprofit domain

attributes.name: governing_psea_policy_id

attributes.name: implementing_org_unit_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the organizational unit (country office, regional office, or headquarters division) responsible for implementing this intervention.

attributes.name: primary_system_platform_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to technology.system_platform. Business justification: Programs track primary digital platforms supporting implementation (KoboToolbox for surveys, CommCare for case management, DHIS2 for health data). Essential for M&E operations, data quality audits, an

attributes.name: staff_member_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the staff member serving as the primary program manager or chief of party for this intervention, accountable for overall delivery and results.

attributes.name: actual_end_date
attributes.description: Actual date when intervention activities concluded. May differ from planned end date due to extensions, early termination, or operational adjustments.

attributes.name: actual_start_date
attributes.description: Actual date when intervention activities commenced in the field. May differ from planned start date due to delays in funding, security clearances, or operational readiness.

attributes.name: budget_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the total budget amount (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: chs_compliant
attributes.description: Indicates whether the intervention design and implementation plan adhere to the Core Humanitarian Standard on Quality and Accountability, covering nine commitments from needs assessment through accountability to affected populations.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this intervention record was first created in the system, representing when the intervention was registered or entered into the program management system.

attributes.name: disability_inclusion_marker_score
attributes.description: Score indicating the level of disability inclusion in the intervention design and implementation. 0: not disability inclusive; 1: disability visible; 2: disability integrated; 3: disability targeted; 4: disability transformative.

attributes.name: do_no_harm_assessment_completed
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Do No Harm analysis was conducted to identify and mitigate potential negative impacts of the intervention on conflict dynamics, social cohesion, or vulnerable groups.
attributes.references: Do No Harm Framework, CHS Protection Principles

attributes.name: environmental_impact_assessment_completed
attributes.description: Indicates whether an environmental impact assessment was conducted to evaluate and mitigate potential environmental harm from intervention activities (e.g., water extraction, waste disposal, construction).
attributes.references: IASC Environmental Marker, Sphere Environmental Health Standards

attributes.name: gender_marker_score
attributes.description: IASC Gender Marker score indicating the extent to which the intervention integrates gender equality. 0: no gender integration; 1: contributes to gender equality; 2a: has gender equality as a significant objective; 2b: has gender equality as the principal objective.

attributes.name: geographic_scope
attributes.description: Geographic coverage level of the intervention. National: entire country; Regional: multiple provinces/states; District: specific administrative districts; Community: village or neighborhood level; Multi-country: cross-border or regional program.

attributes.name: intervention_code
attributes.description: Externally-known unique business identifier for the intervention, used in donor reporting, grant proposals, and field operations. Often follows organizational or donor-specific coding conventions.

attributes.name: intervention_name
attributes.description: Full descriptive name of the intervention as it appears in grant proposals, donor reports, and public communications.

attributes.name: intervention_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the intervention. Pipeline: concept or proposal stage; Approved: funding secured, not yet started; Active: implementation underway; Suspended: temporarily paused; Completed: activities finished, closeout pending; Closed: fully closed out with final reports submitted.
attributes.references: IATI Activity Status, PMD Pro Guide

attributes.name: intervention_type
attributes.description: Classification of the intervention based on its primary purpose and timeframe. Emergency response interventions address immediate humanitarian crises; development interventions focus on long-term sustainable change; recovery interventions bridge emergency and development; resilience interventions build capacity to withstand future shocks; advocacy interventions influence policy and systems; capacity building interventions strengthen partner organizations.
attributes.references: IASC Humanitarian Programme Cycle, OECD DAC Purpose Codes

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this intervention record was last updated, capturing any changes to intervention details, status, or metadata.

attributes.name: logframe_document_url
attributes.description: URL or file path to the intervention's Logical Framework Matrix document, which details the intervention logic, indicators, means of verification, and assumptions.

attributes.name: logic
attributes.description: Structured description of the intervention's logical framework (LogFrame): how activities will produce outputs, how outputs will lead to outcomes, and how outcomes will contribute to impact. Includes key assumptions and risks at each level.

attributes.name: mel_plan_document_url
attributes.business_glossary_term: Monitoring Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Plan Document URL
attributes.description: URL or file path to the intervention's MEL plan, which outlines the monitoring framework, evaluation schedule, data collection methods, and learning agenda.
attributes.references: OECD DAC Evaluation Standards, CHS Commitment 7

attributes.name: phase
attributes.description: Current operational phase within the intervention lifecycle. Design: developing ToC, LogFrame, and proposal; Startup: mobilizing resources, recruiting staff, establishing field presence; Implementation: delivering activities and services; Closeout: finalizing activities, conducting evaluations, submitting final reports.
attributes.references: PMD Pro Guide, Humanitarian Programme Cycle

attributes.name: planned_end_date
attributes.description: Originally planned end date for intervention activities as documented in the grant agreement or project proposal.

attributes.name: planned_start_date
attributes.description: Originally planned start date for intervention activities as documented in the grant agreement or project proposal.

attributes.name: rbm_framework_applied
attributes.description: Indicates whether the intervention applies a formal Results-Based Management framework with defined inputs, activities, outputs, outcomes, and impact, along with indicators and targets at each level.
attributes.references: OECD DAC RBM Principles, UNDG RBM Handbook

attributes.name: safeguarding_policy_applied
attributes.description: Indicates whether the intervention implements organizational safeguarding policies to prevent sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEAH) and protect vulnerable populations, particularly children and women.

attributes.name: sdg_alignment_type
attributes.description: Nature of the intervention's contribution to the SDG. Direct: intervention activities directly advance the SDG indicator; Indirect: intervention creates conditions that support SDG progress; Enabling: intervention builds capacity or systems that enable others to advance the SDG.

attributes.name: sdg_contribution_narrative
attributes.description: Qualitative description of how the intervention contributes to the identified SDG goal, target, and indicator. Articulates the causal pathway and expected magnitude of contribution.

attributes.name: sdg_goal_primary
attributes.description: Primary UN Sustainable Development Goal that this intervention contributes to, expressed as SDG number (e.g., SDG1 for No Poverty, SDG3 for Good Health and Well-being, SDG6 for Clean Water and Sanitation).

attributes.name: sdg_indicator_primary
attributes.description: Specific SDG indicator used to measure the intervention's contribution to the primary target (e.g., 6.1.1 for proportion of population using safely managed drinking water services).

attributes.name: sdg_target_primary
attributes.description: Specific SDG target within the primary goal that this intervention addresses (e.g., 6.1 for universal access to safe drinking water, 3.8 for universal health coverage).

attributes.name: sector
attributes.description: Primary humanitarian or development sector of the intervention. WASH (Water Sanitation and Hygiene), health, nutrition, education, protection (including GBV and child protection), shelter/NFI, livelihoods, and food security are the most common sectors aligned with Sphere standards and cluster coordination mechanisms. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: wash|health|nutrition|education|protection|shelter|livelihoods|food_security — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IASC Cluster System, OECD DAC Sector Codes, Sphere Humanitarian Charter

attributes.name: short_name
attributes.description: Abbreviated or acronym version of the intervention name used for internal reference and field operations.

attributes.name: situation_analysis
attributes.description: Detailed analysis of the humanitarian or development context that justifies the intervention. Includes needs assessment findings, vulnerability analysis, root causes of the problem, and gaps in existing services or coverage.
attributes.references: Humanitarian Programme Cycle, PMD Pro Guide

attributes.name: sphere_standards_applied
attributes.description: Indicates whether the intervention applies Sphere Humanitarian Charter and Minimum Standards in Humanitarian Response, including protection principles and technical standards for WASH, food security, shelter, and health.

attributes.name: sub_sector
attributes.description: Detailed sub-classification within the primary sector. For example, within WASH: water supply, sanitation facilities, hygiene promotion; within health: primary health care, maternal health, mental health and PSS; within protection: GBV prevention and response, child protection, mine action.
attributes.references: IASC Cluster System, Sphere Technical Standards

attributes.name: sustainability_plan
attributes.description: Strategy for ensuring that intervention benefits and capacities endure beyond the project period. Includes plans for local ownership, capacity building, resource mobilization, policy advocacy, and transition or exit strategies.
attributes.references: OECD DAC Sustainability Criterion, CHS Commitment 9

attributes.name: target_beneficiary_count
attributes.description: Total number of direct beneficiaries the intervention aims to reach, as documented in the project proposal and LogFrame. Represents unique individuals or households, depending on the intervention's unit of analysis.

attributes.name: target_beneficiary_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measurement for target beneficiaries. Individuals: unique persons; Households: family units; Communities: villages or settlements; Institutions: schools, health facilities, or organizations.

attributes.name: targeting_strategy
attributes.description: Methodology and criteria for identifying and selecting beneficiaries. Describes vulnerability criteria, geographic targeting, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and mechanisms to ensure equitable access and prevent exclusion errors.

attributes.name: theory_of_change_narrative
attributes.description: Comprehensive narrative describing the intervention's Theory of Change: the causal pathway from inputs and activities through outputs, outcomes, and impact. Articulates assumptions, preconditions, and the logic connecting intervention activities to intended long-term change.
attributes.references: OECD DAC Evaluation Criteria, PMD Pro Guide

attributes.name: total_budget_amount
attributes.description: Total approved budget for the intervention across all funding sources, expressed in the organization's reporting currency. Includes direct program costs, indirect costs, and any cost-sharing or in-kind contributions.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200, IATI Budget

products.name: theory_of_change
products.description: Captures the Theory of Change (ToC) for each program intervention, documenting the causal logic linking inputs, activities, outputs, outcomes, and impact. Stores narrative ToC statements, assumptions, risks, enabling conditions, and linkages to SDGs and humanitarian principles. Supports RBM (Results-Based Management) and donor reporting requirements. One ToC record per program version, with versioning to track revisions across program cycles.
products.reference: OECD DAC Theory of Change; USAID Program Cycle Guidance

attributes.name: theory_of_change_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the Theory of Change record. Primary key.

attributes.name: approved_by_staff_member_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Approved By Staff Member Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.staff_member. Business justification: Theory of change approval requires tracking the authorizing staff member for governance, audit trails, and donor compliance reporting. Standard nonprofit program design workflow.

attributes.name: chs_self_assessment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.chs_self_assessment. Business justification: Theory of Change provides evidence for CHS Commitment 1 (humanitarian standards) and Commitment 2 (effective response). Essential for linking program design to CHS compliance verification.

attributes.name: intervention_id
attributes.description: Reference to the program intervention this Theory of Change supports. Links to the program master data.

attributes.name: activity_statement
attributes.description: Summary of the key actions and interventions the program will undertake to produce outputs. Describes what the program does.
attributes.references: Results-Based Management (RBM) Framework, Logical Framework (LogFrame) Approach

attributes.name: approved_date
attributes.description: Date on which this Theory of Change version was formally approved for use.

attributes.name: assumptions
attributes.description: Critical assumptions underlying the causal logic of the Theory of Change. Conditions believed to be true for the intervention logic to hold, but not directly controlled by the program.
attributes.references: Results-Based Management (RBM) Framework, Logical Framework (LogFrame) Approach

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this Theory of Change record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: do_no_harm_considerations
attributes.description: Analysis of potential unintended negative consequences of the intervention and mitigation strategies. Ensures the program does not exacerbate vulnerabilities or create harm.
attributes.references: Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS), Do No Harm Framework

attributes.name: donor_requirements
attributes.description: Specific donor-mandated requirements or frameworks that this Theory of Change must satisfy. May include reporting formats, result frameworks, or compliance standards.
attributes.references: Grant Management Standards, Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200

attributes.name: enabling_conditions
attributes.description: External factors and preconditions necessary for the Theory of Change to succeed. Contextual elements that facilitate or hinder the intervention logic.

attributes.name: gender_integration_approach
attributes.description: Description of how gender considerations and Gender-Based Violence (GBV) prevention are integrated into the Theory of Change. Documents gender-sensitive or gender-transformative elements.
attributes.references: Gender-Based Violence (GBV) Prevention Standards, Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS)

attributes.name: geographic_scope
attributes.description: Geographic coverage and boundaries of the intervention described in the Theory of Change. May include countries, regions, districts, or specific project sites.

attributes.name: humanitarian_principles_alignment
attributes.description: Description of how the Theory of Change adheres to core humanitarian principles: humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence.
attributes.references: Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS), Sphere Humanitarian Charter

attributes.name: impact_statement
attributes.description: High-level statement of the ultimate long-term change the program aims to achieve. Represents the apex of the results chain in the Theory of Change.
attributes.references: Results-Based Management (RBM) Framework, Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) Framework

attributes.name: input_statement
attributes.description: Description of the resources (financial, human, material) required to implement activities. Foundation of the results chain.
attributes.references: Results-Based Management (RBM) Framework, Logical Framework (LogFrame) Approach

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this Theory of Change record was last updated in the system.

attributes.name: logframe_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier or link to the associated Logical Framework matrix that operationalizes this Theory of Change with indicators, means of verification, and assumptions.

attributes.name: mel_framework_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Monitoring Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Framework Reference
attributes.description: Reference to the MEL or MEAL framework that defines how the Theory of Change will be monitored, evaluated, and adapted based on learning.

attributes.name: outcome_statement
attributes.description: Description of the medium-term changes in behavior, relationships, actions, or conditions that the program seeks to influence. Intermediate results leading to impact.
attributes.references: Results-Based Management (RBM) Framework, Logical Framework (LogFrame) Approach

attributes.name: output_statement
attributes.description: Description of the direct products, goods, and services delivered by program activities. Tangible deliverables under program control.
attributes.references: Results-Based Management (RBM) Framework, Logical Framework (LogFrame) Approach

attributes.name: revision_reason
attributes.description: Explanation of why this Theory of Change was revised from a previous version. Documents adaptive management and learning.
attributes.references: Results-Based Management (RBM) Framework, Monitoring Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Standards

attributes.name: risks
attributes.description: Identified risks and threats that could disrupt the causal pathway or prevent achievement of intended results. Includes contextual, operational, and external risks.
attributes.references: Results-Based Management (RBM) Framework, Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS)

attributes.name: sdg_alignment
attributes.description: Mapping of the Theory of Change to relevant United Nations Sustainable Development Goals and targets. Documents contribution to global development agenda.
attributes.references: United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) Framework

attributes.name: sector_classification
attributes.description: Primary humanitarian or development sector(s) this Theory of Change addresses (e.g., WASH, Health, Nutrition, Education, Protection, Livelihoods). May reference DAC sector codes or cluster classifications.
attributes.references: Development Assistance Committee (DAC) Sector Classification, Inter-Agency Standing Committee (IASC) Cluster System

attributes.name: stakeholder_engagement_approach
attributes.description: Description of how stakeholders (beneficiaries, partners, communities, government) were engaged in developing and validating the Theory of Change. Reflects participatory design principles.
attributes.references: Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS), Humanitarian Accountability Partnership (HAP) Standards

attributes.name: target_population
attributes.description: Description of the primary beneficiary population the Theory of Change aims to serve. May include demographic characteristics, vulnerability profiles, and geographic scope.
attributes.references: Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS), Sphere Humanitarian Charter

attributes.name: timeframe_end_date
attributes.description: Planned end date for the intervention period covered by this Theory of Change. Marks the target completion of the results chain.

attributes.name: timeframe_start_date
attributes.description: Planned start date for the intervention period covered by this Theory of Change. Marks the beginning of the results chain timeline.

attributes.name: toc_narrative
attributes.description: Comprehensive narrative describing the causal logic linking inputs, activities, outputs, outcomes, and long-term impact. Articulates how and why the intervention is expected to achieve its goals.
attributes.references: Results-Based Management (RBM) Framework, Logical Framework (LogFrame) Approach

attributes.name: toc_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the Theory of Change document. Tracks progression from draft through approval to active use and eventual archival.

attributes.name: toc_title
attributes.description: Descriptive title of the Theory of Change, summarizing the intervention logic and intended impact pathway.

attributes.name: toc_version_number
attributes.description: Version identifier for this Theory of Change iteration. Supports tracking revisions across program cycles (e.g., 1.0, 1.1, 2.0).

products.name: program_logframe
products.description: Logical Framework (LogFrame) matrix for a program intervention, including the structured hierarchy of goal, purpose/outcome, outputs, and activities at the row level. Each row captures result statement, indicator reference, baseline value, target value, means of verification (MoV), assumptions, responsible unit, and reporting frequency. Supports RBM and is the primary planning artifact used in grant proposals and donor agreements. Linked to the Theory of Change and MEL indicator library. Versioned to track amendments across program lifecycle.
products.reference: OECD DAC LogFrame; EC PRAG Logical Framework Approach

attributes.name: program_logframe_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the program logical framework row entry. Primary key for the LogFrame matrix.

attributes.name: approved_by_staff_member_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Approved By Staff Member Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.staff_member. Business justification: Logframe approval authority must be traceable to specific staff for donor reporting, audit compliance, and results-based management accountability in nonprofit operations.

attributes.name: chs_self_assessment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.chs_self_assessment. Business justification: Logframe provides evidence for CHS Commitment 5 (complaints mechanism indicators) and Commitment 6 (coordinated response). Essential for linking M&E framework to CHS compliance verification.

attributes.name: intervention_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent program intervention to which this LogFrame row belongs.

attributes.name: amendment_reason
attributes.description: Explanation for why this LogFrame row was revised or amended (e.g., donor request, context change, program adaptation, no-cost extension).

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which this LogFrame row or version was formally approved for implementation and reporting.

attributes.name: assumptions
attributes.description: External conditions or factors that must hold true for the result to be achieved but are outside the programs direct control.

attributes.name: baseline_date
attributes.description: The date on which the baseline value was measured or established.

attributes.name: baseline_value
attributes.description: The initial measured value of the indicator at program start, serving as the reference point for progress measurement.
attributes.references: Monitoring Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Standards, Results-Based Management (RBM)

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this LogFrame row record was first created in the system.
attributes.references: Data Governance Standards, Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: dac_sector_code
attributes.description: The five-digit OECD Development Assistance Committee sector code classifying the type of aid activity (e.g., 14030 for water supply and sanitation).
attributes.references: OECD Development Assistance Committee (DAC) Sector Classification

attributes.name: data_collection_method
attributes.description: The primary methodology used to collect indicator data (e.g., household survey, Focus Group Discussion (FGD), Key Informant Interview (KII), administrative records, mobile data collection).

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: The specific system, database, or organizational unit that provides the indicator data (e.g., DHIS2, KoboToolbox, field office reports).

attributes.name: disaggregation_dimensions
attributes.description: The demographic or geographic dimensions by which indicator data should be disaggregated for equity analysis (e.g., sex, age group, disability status, geographic location).
attributes.references: Monitoring Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Standards, Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS)

attributes.name: donor_visibility_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this result is included in external donor reports and dashboards (True) or is for internal use only (False).
attributes.references: Donor Reporting Requirements, Grant Management Standards

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The date on which this LogFrame row version is superseded by a new version or the program closes. Null for currently active versions.
attributes.references: Results-Based Management (RBM) Standards, Version Control Standards

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The date from which this LogFrame row version becomes active and applicable for monitoring and reporting.
attributes.references: Results-Based Management (RBM) Standards, Version Control Standards

attributes.name: grant_requirement_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this LogFrame row is a mandatory reporting requirement specified in the donor grant agreement (True) or an internal monitoring element (False).
attributes.references: Grant Management Standards, Donor Reporting Requirements

attributes.name: hierarchy_level
attributes.description: The hierarchical tier of this LogFrame row within the results chain: goal (impact), purpose/outcome, output, or activity.
attributes.references: Results-Based Management (RBM) Standards, Logical Framework Approach (LFA)

attributes.name: indicator_reference_code
attributes.description: Code or identifier linking this LogFrame row to the corresponding indicator in the Monitoring Evaluation and Learning (MEL) indicator library.
attributes.references: Monitoring Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Standards, Results-Based Management (RBM)

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this LogFrame row record was most recently updated.
attributes.references: Data Governance Standards, Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: means_of_verification
attributes.description: The data sources and methods used to verify achievement of the result (e.g., household surveys, administrative records, Post-Distribution Monitoring (PDM), Key Informant Interviews (KII)).
attributes.references: Logical Framework Approach (LFA), Monitoring Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Standards

attributes.name: mitigation_strategy
attributes.description: The planned actions or contingency measures to reduce the likelihood or impact of risks to achieving this result.
attributes.references: Results-Based Management (RBM) Standards, Risk Management Framework

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional contextual information, clarifications, or implementation guidance related to this LogFrame row.

attributes.name: program_logframe_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this LogFrame row indicating progress and health (draft during proposal, active during implementation, achieved/not_achieved at closeout). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|active|on_track|at_risk|delayed|achieved|not_achieved|archived — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Results-Based Management (RBM) Standards, Program Lifecycle Management

attributes.name: reporting_frequency
attributes.description: The cadence at which progress against this LogFrame row is measured and reported to donors and stakeholders.
attributes.references: Monitoring Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Standards, Donor Reporting Requirements

attributes.name: responsible_unit
attributes.description: The organizational unit, department, or team accountable for delivering this result (e.g., WASH team, Health program unit, Field Operations).
attributes.references: Results-Based Management (RBM) Standards, RACI (Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed) Framework

attributes.name: result_statement
attributes.description: Narrative description of the intended result at this hierarchy level (goal, outcome, output, or activity statement).
attributes.references: Results-Based Management (RBM) Standards, Logical Framework Approach (LFA)

attributes.name: risk_level
attributes.description: The assessed level of risk that this result may not be achieved due to internal or external factors.
attributes.references: Results-Based Management (RBM) Standards, Risk Management Framework

attributes.name: row_sequence_number
attributes.description: Ordinal position of this row within the LogFrame matrix for display and reporting purposes.

attributes.name: sdg_alignment
attributes.description: The United Nations Sustainable Development Goal(s) and target(s) to which this result contributes (e.g., SDG 6.1, SDG 3.2).

attributes.name: sector_classification
attributes.description: The humanitarian or development sector to which this result belongs (e.g., WASH (Water Sanitation and Hygiene), Health, Nutrition, Education, Protection, Livelihoods). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: wash|health|nutrition|education|protection|livelihoods|shelter|food_security|early_recovery — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Development Assistance Committee (DAC) Sector Codes, Inter-Agency Standing Committee (IASC) Cluster System

attributes.name: target_date
attributes.description: The date by which the target value is expected to be achieved, typically the program end date or milestone date.

attributes.name: target_value
attributes.description: The intended end-of-program value for the indicator, representing the planned achievement level.
attributes.references: Results-Based Management (RBM) Standards, Monitoring Evaluation and Learning (MEL)

attributes.name: theory_of_change_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier linking this LogFrame row to the corresponding pathway or assumption in the programs Theory of Change (ToC) diagram.
attributes.references: Results-Based Management (RBM) Standards, Theory of Change Methodology

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: The measurement unit for baseline and target values (e.g., number of beneficiaries, percentage, households, liters).

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version identifier for the LogFrame matrix to track amendments and revisions across the program lifecycle (e.g., 1.0, 1.1, 2.0).

products.name: logframe_row

attributes.name: parent_result_logframe_row_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent result row in the LogFrame hierarchy. Enables navigation of the results chain (e.g., linking an output to its parent outcome).

attributes.name: program_logframe_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent LogFrame document to which this row belongs. Links this row to the overall program LogFrame structure.

attributes.name: assumptions
attributes.description: External conditions or factors that must hold true for this result to be achieved but are outside the program's direct control. Critical for risk management and adaptive management.

attributes.name: baseline_date
attributes.description: The date when the baseline value was measured or established. Critical for understanding the timeframe of change.

attributes.name: baseline_value
attributes.description: The starting value or condition for the indicator before program intervention. Provides the reference point for measuring change. Stored as string to accommodate numeric, text, or mixed values.

attributes.name: beneficiary_target_count

attributes.references: Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS), Monitoring Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Framework

attributes.name: budget_allocated

attributes.references: Grant Management System (GMS), Budget Management Standard

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this LogFrame row entry was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the budget allocated to this result (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: dac_code
attributes.description: The OECD DAC sector or purpose code assigned to this result. Enables standardized international development reporting.
attributes.references: OECD Development Assistance Committee (DAC) Sector Codes

attributes.name: data_collection_method
