products.name: program_partnership
products.description: This association product represents the formal partnership agreement between a humanitarian/development intervention and a partner organization. It captures the specific role, responsibilities, budget allocation, performance metrics, and compliance status for each partner's involvement in each intervention. Each record links one intervention to one partner organization with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific partnership arrangement.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit humanitarian operations, interventions are routinely implemented through multi-partner consortia where a single intervention engages multiple partner organizations (lead implementer, sub-recipients, local CBOs, technical specialists) each with distinct roles, geographic coverage, and budget allocations. Simultaneously, established partner organizations implement multiple interventions across different sectors and geographies. The partnership arrangement itself is an operational business entity that program managers actively create, monitor, and close out, with specific attributes like role, budget allocation, performance rating, compliance status, and risk assessment that belong to neither the intervention nor the partner organization alone.

attributes.name: program_partnership_id
attributes.description: Primary key for the partnership association

attributes.name: intervention_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the intervention that this partnership supports

attributes.name: partner_org_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the partner organization participating in this intervention

attributes.name: beneficiary_target_count
attributes.description: Number of beneficiaries this partner is responsible for reaching within this intervention. Sum of all partner beneficiary targets should equal the intervention's total target beneficiary count.

attributes.name: budget_allocated_amount
attributes.description: Total budget amount allocated to this partner for their scope of work in this intervention. Sum of all partner budget allocations should equal or be less than the intervention's total budget.

attributes.name: capacity_assessment_status
attributes.description: Result of the capacity assessment conducted specifically for this partner's role in this intervention. May differ from the partner's general organizational capacity assessment.

attributes.name: compliance_status
attributes.description: Current compliance status of this partner for this intervention against contractual obligations, donor regulations, and organizational policies. Tracks whether the partner is meeting reporting, financial, and programmatic requirements.

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: Date when this partner completed or will complete their scope of work for this intervention. May differ from the intervention's overall end date if partners have staggered timelines.

attributes.name: geographic_scope
attributes.description: Specific geographic area (region, district, or community) where this partner is responsible for implementing activities within the broader intervention geography. Allows multiple partners to cover different areas of the same intervention.

attributes.name: partnership_role
attributes.description: The specific role this partner plays in the intervention (e.g., Lead Implementer, Sub-Recipient, Technical Partner, Local CBO, Consortium Member). Defines the partner's primary responsibility and authority level.

attributes.name: partnership_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this specific partnership arrangement within the intervention. Tracks whether the partner is actively implementing, suspended due to performance issues, or completed their scope of work.

attributes.name: partnership_type
attributes.description: Classification of the partnership arrangement type (e.g., Direct Implementation, Sub-Award, Technical Assistance, Capacity Building, Coordination). Determines reporting and compliance requirements.

attributes.name: performance_rating
attributes.description: Performance assessment rating for this partner's work on this specific intervention. Based on delivery against milestones, budget utilization, reporting quality, and beneficiary feedback.

attributes.name: reporting_frequency
attributes.description: Required frequency for this partner to submit progress reports for this intervention. Determined by risk rating, budget size, and donor requirements.

attributes.name: risk_rating
attributes.description: Risk level assigned to this specific partnership based on partner capacity, geographic context, budget size, and intervention complexity. Determines oversight and monitoring intensity.

attributes.name: sector_focus
attributes.description: Specific sector or sub-sector within the intervention that this partner is responsible for. Relevant for multi-sectoral interventions where different partners handle different technical areas (e.g., one partner for WASH, another for nutrition).

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: Date when this partner began implementation activities for this intervention. May differ from the intervention's overall start date if partners were phased in.

attributes.name: sub_award_reference
attributes.description: Unique reference number for the sub-award agreement or MoU governing this partnership. Links to legal/contractual documentation.

products.name: intervention_compliance
products.description: This association product represents the compliance obligation between a humanitarian intervention and a specific donor requirement. It captures the requirement-specific compliance status, deadlines, submission tracking, and responsible staff for each intervention-requirement pair. Each record links one intervention to one donor compliance requirement with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific compliance obligation.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit grant management, a single humanitarian intervention (e.g., a WASH program) must fulfill multiple donor compliance requirements (quarterly narrative reports, financial statements, evaluations, audit submissions) imposed by one or more institutional donors funding that intervention. Conversely, a single donor compliance requirement type (e.g., quarterly narrative report format) applies to multiple interventions funded by that donor. Compliance teams actively manage each intervention-requirement pair with specific deadlines, submission tracking, approval status, responsible staff assignments, and waiver requests.

attributes.name: intervention_compliance_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this intervention-specific compliance obligation record. Primary key.

attributes.name: donor_requirement_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Intervention Compliance - Donor Compliance Req Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the specific donor compliance requirement that applies to this intervention

attributes.name: intervention_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the humanitarian intervention that must fulfill this compliance requirement

attributes.name: responsible_staff_member_id
attributes.description: Reference to the staff member assigned primary responsibility for ensuring compliance with this requirement for this specific intervention. May differ from the general staff_member_id in donor_requirement if intervention-specific ownership applies.

attributes.name: actual_effort_hours
attributes.description: The actual number of staff hours expended in fulfilling this compliance requirement for this specific intervention.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the donor formally approved or accepted the compliance submission for this intervention.

attributes.name: associated_cost_amount
attributes.description: The direct financial cost incurred to fulfill this compliance requirement for this specific intervention (e.g., audit fees, consultant costs, translation services).

attributes.name: cost_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the associated cost amount.

attributes.name: created_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this intervention-compliance obligation record was created in the system.

attributes.name: deliverable_format
attributes.description: The required format or medium for the compliance deliverable for this intervention (e.g., PDF report, Excel workbook, online portal submission).

attributes.name: due_date
attributes.description: The date by which this compliance requirement must be fulfilled for this specific intervention. May differ from the general due_date in donor_requirement if intervention-specific extensions or schedules apply.

attributes.name: last_modified_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this intervention-compliance obligation record was last updated.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional free-text notes, comments, or context related to this compliance requirement for this specific intervention.

attributes.name: requirement_status
attributes.description: Current status of compliance with this specific requirement for this specific intervention. Tracks the intervention-specific compliance state, distinct from the general requirement status in donor_requirement.

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: The actual date on which the compliance deliverable for this intervention was submitted to the donor.

attributes.name: waiver_granted_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the donor has approved a waiver or exemption for this compliance requirement specifically for this intervention.

attributes.name: waiver_justification
attributes.description: The rationale or explanation provided for requesting a waiver from this compliance requirement for this specific intervention.

products.name: component_indicator
products.description: This association product represents the assignment of MEL indicators to program components for monitoring and evaluation purposes. It captures component-specific measurement targets, baselines, data collection methods, and reporting responsibilities that exist only in the context of a specific component-indicator pairing. Each record links one program component to one indicator with the specific measurement parameters for that component.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit program management, program components (e.g., WASH water supply, sanitation, hygiene promotion sub-components) are each measured by multiple MEL indicators, and indicators (especially cross-cutting ones like gender equality markers, safeguarding compliance, beneficiary satisfaction) apply across multiple components. MEL teams actively manage the component-indicator matrix in LogFrames, setting component-specific targets, baselines, and data collection methods for each pairing. This is the operational reality of results-based management in the nonprofit sector.

attributes.name: component_indicator_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this component-indicator assignment. Primary key.

attributes.name: component_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the program component being measured

attributes.name: indicator_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the MEL indicator used for measurement

attributes.name: assignment_date
attributes.description: The date when this indicator was assigned to this component for monitoring. Tracks when the measurement relationship was established.

attributes.name: baseline_value
attributes.description: The baseline value for this indicator measured at the start of this component. Component-level baselines may differ from program-level baselines due to geographic or population differences.

attributes.name: component_indicator_status
attributes.description: Current status of this component-indicator assignment. Indicates whether this indicator is actively being measured for this component.

attributes.name: data_collection_method
attributes.description: The specific data collection method used for this indicator within this component (e.g., household survey, facility assessment, DHIS2 extraction, beneficiary registration). May differ from the indicator master method based on component context and available systems.

attributes.name: is_mandatory
attributes.description: Indicates whether this indicator is mandatory for this component due to donor requirements, grant agreements, or regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: logframe_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the specific output, outcome, or result in the component's LogFrame that this indicator measures. Links the indicator to the component's theory of change.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes about this specific component-indicator assignment, including context, challenges, or special considerations for measurement.

attributes.name: reporting_frequency
attributes.description: How often this indicator must be reported for this specific component. May differ from the indicator master reporting frequency based on donor requirements or component risk level.

attributes.name: responsible_unit
attributes.description: The organizational unit, team, or field office responsible for collecting and reporting data for this indicator within this component. Assigns accountability at the component level.

attributes.name: target_value
attributes.description: The target value for this indicator specific to this component. May differ from the program-level or indicator master target because each component contributes differently to overall program goals.

products.name: component_system_usage
products.description: This association product represents the operational usage relationship between program components and digital platforms. It captures which systems are actively used to deliver, monitor, or report on specific program components, including the functional role of each system, access permissions, and usage lifecycle dates. Each record links one component to one system platform with attributes that exist only in the context of this operational usage relationship.. Existence Justification: In NGO operations, program components routinely use multiple specialized digital systems simultaneously (e.g., a health component uses DHIS2 for health data, KoboToolbox for field surveys, and Salesforce for beneficiary tracking). Conversely, enterprise systems like Salesforce or DHIS2 serve multiple components across different programs and sectors. The business actively manages these usage relationships, tracking which systems support which components, provisioning access for component teams, and managing activation/deactivation as components evolve.

attributes.name: component_system_usage_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this component-system usage relationship. Primary key.

attributes.name: component_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the program component that uses this system platform

attributes.name: system_platform_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Component System Usage - System Platform Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the system platform used by this component

attributes.name: activation_date
attributes.description: Date when this system was activated for use by this component. Tracks the start of the usage relationship. Explicitly identified in detection phase.

attributes.name: component_system_role
attributes.description: The functional role this system plays for this specific component (e.g., Data Collection for KoboToolbox in a WASH component, Beneficiary Management for Salesforce in a cash transfer component). Explicitly identified in detection phase.

attributes.name: data_classification_level
attributes.description: The highest data classification level of information that this component stores or processes in this specific system. May vary by component-system combination (e.g., a health component may store PII in DHIS2 while an infrastructure component stores only public data in the same system). Explicitly identified in detection phase.

attributes.name: deactivation_date
attributes.description: Date when this system was deactivated or stopped being used by this component. Null if still active. Tracks the end of the usage relationship. Explicitly identified in detection phase.

attributes.name: integration_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this component requires data integration or synchronization between this system and other systems in the component's technology stack.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes about this component-system usage relationship, including special configurations, access restrictions, or usage patterns.

attributes.name: primary_contact
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the individual responsible for managing this system usage for this component (e.g., component MEL officer, data focal point).

attributes.name: usage_status
attributes.description: Current status of this component-system usage relationship (Active, Inactive, Pilot, Sunset, Decommissioned). Tracks the lifecycle of the usage relationship independently from the component or system status.

attributes.name: user_access_count
attributes.description: Number of users from this component team who have active access to this system platform. Tracks component-specific system access provisioning. Explicitly identified in detection phase.

products.name: program
products.description: Master reference table for program. Referenced by program_id.

attributes.name: program_id
attributes.description: Primary key for program

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when the program proposal was formally approved by internal governance or donor.

attributes.name: budget_amount
attributes.description: Total approved budget for the program across all funding sources in the program's base currency.

attributes.name: budget_currency
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the program budget.

attributes.name: closeout_date
attributes.description: Date when all program activities, financial reconciliation, and final reporting were completed.

attributes.name: cluster_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the humanitarian cluster or sector coordination mechanism the program is aligned with (e.g., WASH, Health, Protection).

attributes.name: compliance_status
attributes.description: Current compliance standing with donor requirements, regulatory obligations, and internal policies.

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code for the primary country of program implementation.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the program record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: donor_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the primary donor or funding organization for this program.

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: Planned or actual end date when program activities conclude and closeout begins.

attributes.name: geographic_scope
attributes.description: Spatial scale of program implementation indicating coverage area.

attributes.name: grant_number
attributes.description: Unique grant or award number assigned by the donor for tracking and reporting purposes.

attributes.name: humanitarian_response_plan_id
attributes.description: Identifier linking the program to a coordinated Humanitarian Response Plan or Flash Appeal.

attributes.name: implementing_partner_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the primary implementing partner organization responsible for program execution.

attributes.name: is_emergency
attributes.description: Indicates whether the program is classified as an emergency response intervention requiring expedited procedures.

attributes.name: is_multi_year
attributes.description: Indicates whether the program spans multiple fiscal years requiring multi-year budgeting and planning.

attributes.name: logframe_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier or document link to the program's Logical Framework Matrix defining objectives, indicators, and assumptions.

attributes.name: modified_by
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the user who last modified the program record.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the program record was last updated in the system.

attributes.name: monitoring_frequency
attributes.description: Scheduled frequency for program monitoring and evaluation activities.

attributes.name: parent_program_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the parent program if this program is part of a larger program hierarchy or portfolio.

attributes.name: program_code
attributes.description: Externally-known unique alphanumeric code assigned to the program for identification across systems and donor reporting.

attributes.name: program_description
attributes.description: Comprehensive narrative describing the program's objectives, scope, target population, and expected outcomes.

attributes.name: program_manager_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the staff member responsible for overall program management and accountability.

attributes.name: program_name
attributes.description: Official name of the humanitarian or development program as registered with donors and governing bodies.

attributes.name: program_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the program indicating its operational state.

attributes.name: program_type
attributes.description: Classification of the program based on its primary intervention approach and duration.

attributes.name: region
attributes.description: Geographic region or administrative area within the country where the program operates.

attributes.name: reporting_frequency
attributes.description: Required frequency for submitting progress and financial reports to donors and stakeholders.

attributes.name: risk_rating
attributes.description: Overall risk assessment level for the program considering contextual, operational, financial, and reputational risks.

attributes.name: sdg_alignment
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of SDG goal numbers (1-17) and targets that the program contributes to.

attributes.name: sector_code
attributes.description: Five-digit code identifying the primary humanitarian or development sector (WASH, Health, Nutrition, Education, Protection, Livelihood, Shelter, etc.).

attributes.name: sector_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the primary sector in which the program operates.

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: Official start date when program implementation begins as per the approved proposal or agreement.

attributes.name: subsector
attributes.description: More granular classification within the primary sector (e.g., Water Supply, Sanitation, Hygiene Promotion under WASH).

attributes.name: target_beneficiaries
attributes.description: Planned total number of direct beneficiaries the program aims to reach.

attributes.name: target_population
attributes.description: Description of the intended beneficiary population including demographic characteristics, vulnerability criteria, and geographic scope.

attributes.name: theory_of_change
attributes.description: Narrative or structured description of the causal pathway linking program inputs, activities, outputs, outcomes, and impact.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the user who created the program record.

domains.name: grant
domains.description: Authoritative domain for all grant awards, funding agreements, and donor contracts. Manages grant lifecycle from proposal development and submission through award, amendment, budget tracking, compliance, and closeout. Tracks donor conditions, restricted vs. unrestricted funding, NICRA/ICR rates, and compliance obligations under USAID, BHA, DFID, CERF, and OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.

products.name: sub_award_disbursement
products.description: Transactional record for individual fund disbursements made to sub-award implementing partners. Captures disbursement request date, approval date, disbursement amount, currency, exchange rate (for multi-currency operations), disbursement method (wire transfer, mobile money, check), bank transfer reference, advance vs. reimbursement classification, tranche number, liquidation status, liquidation deadline, outstanding advance balance, and supporting documentation reference. Enables BvA (Budget vs. Actual) tracking at the sub-award level and supports 2 CFR 200.305 advance payment requirements.

attributes.name: sub_award_disbursement_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for each sub-award disbursement transaction record in the grant management system.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.305; Unit4 ERP Project Accounting

attributes.name: award_id
attributes.description: Reference to the prime grant award from which this sub-award disbursement is funded. Enables Budget vs. Actual (BvA) tracking at the prime award level.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.305; IATI Standard

attributes.name: budget_line_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific approved budget line item within the sub-award budget against which this disbursement is charged. Enables granular Budget vs. Actual (BvA) variance analysis at the budget line level.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.308; Unit4 ERP Project Accounting

attributes.name: component_id
attributes.description: Reference to the program or project under which this sub-award disbursement is executed. Enables program-level Budget vs. Actual (BvA) tracking and Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) linkage.
attributes.references: IATI Standard; OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200; Unit4 ERP Project Accounting

attributes.name: partner_org_id
attributes.description: Reference to the sub-recipient organization (Community-Based Organization, Civil Society Organization, or other implementing partner) receiving this disbursement.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.331; Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS)

attributes.name: subaward_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent sub-award agreement under which this disbursement is made. Links the disbursement to the specific sub-award instrument and implementing partner.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.331; Unit4 ERP Project Accounting

attributes.name: advance_balance_outstanding
attributes.description: Remaining unliquidated advance balance owed by the implementing partner at the time of this disbursement record. Calculated as cumulative advances disbursed minus cumulative liquidations submitted. Supports 2 CFR 200.305 advance payment monitoring and cash management.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.305; Unit4 ERP Project Accounting

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the authorized approver (grants manager, finance director, or designated authority) formally approved the disbursement request for payment processing.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.305; SAP S/4HANA Accounts Payable

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the authorized staff member (grants manager, finance director, or country director) who approved this disbursement. Required for audit trail and segregation of duties compliance.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.303; Internal Revenue Service 501(c)(3) Regulations

attributes.name: bank_transfer_reference
attributes.description: Bank-issued or payment-system-issued reference number for the wire transfer, EFT, or mobile money transaction. Used for bank reconciliation, audit trail, and confirmation of funds receipt by the implementing partner.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Accounts Payable; OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.305

attributes.name: cost_category
attributes.description: Budget cost category classification for this disbursement per the approved sub-award budget. Supports Budget vs. Actual (BvA) analysis by cost line and compliance with donor-approved budget categories under OMB Uniform Guidance.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.413; USAID ADS Chapter 591

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this disbursement record was first created in the Grant Management System (GMS) or Unit4 ERP. Provides the audit trail creation marker required under OMB Uniform Guidance record retention requirements.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.333; SAP S/4HANA Audit Trail

attributes.name: disbursement_amount
attributes.description: Gross amount disbursed to the implementing partner in the transaction currency. Used as the primary monetary value for Budget vs. Actual (BvA) tracking at the sub-award level.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.305; FASB ASC 958; GAAP for Nonprofits

attributes.name: disbursement_amount_usd
attributes.description: Disbursement amount converted to US Dollars (USD) using the applied exchange rate. Used for consolidated Budget vs. Actual (BvA) reporting, donor financial reports, and NICRA/Indirect Cost Rate (ICR) calculations across multi-currency sub-awards.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200; FASB ASC 830; USAID ADS

attributes.name: disbursement_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code of the currency in which the disbursement was made to the implementing partner (e.g., USD, EUR, KES, NGN). Supports multi-currency operations in international humanitarian programs.
attributes.references: ISO 4217; IATI Standard; OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200

attributes.name: disbursement_date
attributes.description: Actual date on which funds were transferred to the implementing partner's bank account or mobile money wallet. This is the principal business event date for Budget vs. Actual (BvA) reporting and cash flow tracking.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.305; FASB ASC 958; IATI Standard

attributes.name: disbursement_method
attributes.description: Mechanism by which funds are transferred to the implementing partner. Includes wire transfer for international bank transfers, mobile money for field-based digital payments (e.g., M-Pesa), check, cash for remote/emergency contexts, and electronic funds transfer (EFT) for domestic payments.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.305; BHA Standard Terms and Conditions

attributes.name: disbursement_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for grants staff to record contextual notes, special conditions, or explanations related to this disbursement, such as reasons for partial payment, exchange rate justification, or emergency authorization rationale.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.333; Unit4 ERP Project Accounting

attributes.name: disbursement_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique alphanumeric reference number assigned to this disbursement transaction, used in bank transfer instructions, financial records, and audit trails. Corresponds to the payment reference in SAP S/4HANA Accounts Payable.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Accounts Payable; OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.305

attributes.name: disbursement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the disbursement transaction. Tracks progression from draft request through approval, actual disbursement, and final liquidation or cancellation. Drives workflow routing in the Grant Management System (GMS).
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.305; Unit4 ERP Project Accounting

attributes.name: disbursement_type
attributes.description: Classification of the disbursement as an advance payment to the sub-recipient prior to expenditure, a reimbursement for costs already incurred, a direct payment to a third-party vendor on behalf of the sub-recipient, or a letter-of-credit drawdown. Governs compliance with 2 CFR 200.305 advance payment requirements.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.305; USAID ADS Chapter 636

attributes.name: donor_reporting_category
attributes.description: Donor-specific budget category or expenditure classification code required for financial reporting to the prime donor (e.g., USAID, BHA, DFID, CERF). Maps the disbursement to the donor's chart of accounts or budget template for Financial Report (SF-425) or equivalent submission. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product as values vary by donor]
attributes.references: USAID ADS; BHA Standard Terms and Conditions; DFID Smart Rules; CERF Guidelines

attributes.name: exchange_rate
attributes.description: Foreign currency exchange rate applied to convert the disbursement amount from the transaction currency to the base reporting currency (typically USD) at the time of disbursement. Essential for consolidated financial reporting and donor reporting under USAID, BHA, and DFID requirements.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200; FASB ASC 830 Foreign Currency Matters; IATI Standard

attributes.name: fiscal_period
attributes.description: Fiscal accounting period (month number 1–12 within the fiscal year) in which this disbursement is posted to the General Ledger. Supports period-level Budget vs. Actual (BvA) reporting and cash flow forecasting.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 958; SAP S/4HANA General Ledger; GAAP for Nonprofits

attributes.name: fiscal_year
attributes.description: Fiscal year in which this disbursement is recorded for financial reporting purposes. Used for annual financial statement preparation, donor reporting, and compliance with FASB ASC 958 and OMB Uniform Guidance reporting periods.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 958; OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200; GAAP for Nonprofits

attributes.name: fund_restriction_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the disbursed funds are donor-restricted (for a specific purpose or time period), temporarily restricted, or unrestricted. Critical for fund accounting compliance under FASB ASC 958 and donor stewardship reporting.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 958-205; GAAP for Nonprofits; Charity Commission (UK)

attributes.name: gl_account_code
attributes.description: Chart of Accounts (CoA) code in the General Ledger (GL) to which this disbursement is posted. Enables fund accounting, restricted vs. unrestricted fund tracking, and financial statement preparation per FASB ASC 958.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 958; SAP S/4HANA General Ledger; GAAP for Nonprofits

attributes.name: indirect_cost_amount
attributes.description: Calculated indirect cost (Facilities and Administration / F&A) amount included in or associated with this disbursement, based on the NICRA rate applied to the direct cost base. Supports compliance with OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.414 and donor budget monitoring.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.414; NICRA; FASB ASC 958

attributes.name: is_emergency_disbursement
attributes.description: Indicates whether this disbursement was processed as an emergency or expedited payment outside the standard approval workflow, such as for rapid-onset disaster response under CERF or BHA emergency funding mechanisms.
attributes.references: CERF Guidelines; BHA Standard Terms and Conditions; Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS)

attributes.name: liquidated_amount
attributes.description: Amount of the advance disbursement that has been accounted for through submission of eligible expenditure documentation by the implementing partner. The difference between disbursement_amount and liquidated_amount represents the outstanding advance balance.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.305; FASB ASC 958

attributes.name: liquidation_date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the implementing partner submitted the expenditure documentation or financial report fully accounting for the advance disbursement. Null if liquidation is pending or not yet completed.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.305; Unit4 ERP Project Accounting

attributes.name: liquidation_deadline
attributes.description: Contractual deadline by which the implementing partner must submit expenditure documentation (financial report or liquidation report) to account for advance funds disbursed. Compliance with this date is required under 2 CFR 200.305.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.305; BHA Standard Terms and Conditions

attributes.name: liquidation_status
attributes.description: Current status of the liquidation (financial accountability reporting) for this advance disbursement. Tracks whether the implementing partner has submitted expenditure documentation to account for advanced funds per 2 CFR 200.305 requirements.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.305; USAID ADS Chapter 636

attributes.name: net_disbursement_amount
attributes.description: Actual net amount transferred to the implementing partner after deducting any withholding amounts from the gross disbursement amount. This is the amount reflected in the bank transfer instruction.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.305; SAP S/4HANA Accounts Payable; FASB ASC 958

attributes.name: nicra_rate_applied
attributes.business_glossary_term: Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (NICRA) Rate Applied
attributes.description: Indirect Cost Rate (ICR) percentage applied to this disbursement per the implementing partner's Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (NICRA) or approved Facilities and Administration (F&A) rate. Used to calculate allowable indirect costs charged to the sub-award.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.414; NICRA; USAID ADS Chapter 591

attributes.name: payment_terms
attributes.description: Contractual payment terms governing when and how disbursements are made under the sub-award, such as immediate advance, net-30 reimbursement, milestone-based release, or payment upon liquidation of prior advance.
attributes.references: OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.305; Unit4 ERP Project Accounting

attributes.name: post_distribution_monitoring_ref

products.description: SSOT for all donor reporting obligations and submitted reports for each grant award. products.name: award_site_allocation
products.description: This association product represents the operational allocation of grant award funding and activities to specific field project sites. It captures the site-specific budget allocation, activation timeline, beneficiary targets, and implementation roles that exist only in the context of a specific award operating at a specific site. Each record links one award to one project site with attributes that govern site-level financial management, donor reporting, and field operations coordination.. Existence Justification: In humanitarian NGO operations, grant awards routinely fund multi-site programs where a single award supports activities across multiple field locations (health posts, distribution points, WASH facilities), and individual project sites frequently host co-located programming from multiple concurrent awards from different donors. The business actively manages site-specific budget allocations, activation timelines, beneficiary targets, and implementation roles for each award-site combination to support site-level financial tracking and donor reporting requirements.

products.name: asset_allocation
products.description: This association product represents the cost allocation relationship between grant awards and IT assets. It captures the financial assignment of IT asset costs to specific grant awards for compliance reporting, allowable cost verification, and indirect cost allocation. Each record links one award to one IT asset with allocation percentages, cost amounts, and lifecycle dates that exist only in the context of this funding relationship.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit grant management, IT assets are frequently cost-shared across multiple grant awards based on usage allocation (e.g., a server supporting 3 programs, a vehicle used by 2 field offices funded by different donors). Conversely, each grant award funds multiple IT assets over its lifecycle (laptops, software licenses, field equipment). The business actively manages these cost allocation relationships for donor compliance reporting, allowable cost verification under regulations like 2 CFR 200, and indirect cost recovery calculations.

attributes.name: allocation_start_date

products.name: award_position_funding
products.description: This association product represents the funding relationship between grant awards and organizational positions. It captures the split-funding allocation where a single position can be funded by multiple grants simultaneously, and a single grant award funds multiple positions. Each record links one award to one position with the funding percentage, cost allocation amount, funding period, and status that exist only in the context of this specific funding arrangement. This is the operational record used for grant compliance reporting, effort certification, cost allocation, and workforce planning.. Existence Justification: In NGO operations, positions are routinely split-funded across multiple grant awards simultaneously (e.g., one position charged 40% to Award A, 35% to Award B, 25% to Award C), and each grant award funds multiple positions across the organization. This is an operational necessity for grant compliance, effort certification, and cost allocation reporting required by donors under 2 CFR 200 and similar frameworks. The relationship is actively managed by grant managers and finance teams who track effort percentages, funding periods, and cost allocations for each award-position combination.

products.name: grant_staff_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the assignment of staff members to grant awards. It captures the allocation of workforce effort across multiple funding sources, enabling split-effort tracking, cost allocation, and compliance with donor reporting requirements. Each record links one staff member to one award with the specific role, effort percentage, assignment period, and cost allocation method that exist only in the context of this relationship. This is the operational record that HR and grants management teams actively create, update, and monitor throughout the award lifecycle.. Existence Justification: In NGO operations, staff members routinely work across multiple grant awards simultaneously (split effort), and each grant award employs multiple staff members in various roles. The business actively manages these assignments through formal effort allocation processes, tracking the percentage of each staff member's time charged to each award, the role they perform, and the cost allocation method. This is a core operational relationship that HR and grants management teams create, update, and monitor for donor compliance and financial reporting.

products.name: constituent

Represents every entity that gives to or funds the NGO — individual major gift contributors, institutional donors (USAID, DFID/FCDO, UN agencies, DAC members), bilateral and multilateral agencies, private foundations, corporate sponsors, and households. Captures full constituent profile including legal name, preferred name/salutation, constituent type (individual, institutional, foundation, corporate, bilateral, multilateral, household), organization affiliation, IATI organization identifier, communication preferences, GDPR/data consent flags, deceased indicator, ODA eligibility flag, indirect cost rate (ICR/NICRA) terms, preferred grant modality, relationship tier, funder classification (bilateral, multilateral, DAC), country of origin, and CRM source system reference. products.name: gift
products.description: Authoritative transactional ledger and single source of truth for every financial transaction in the donor domain — gifts, donations, matching gifts, tribute gifts, refunds, adjustments, and acknowledgements — processed through Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud and Raisers Edge NXT. This is the ONE table that answers 'what is this donor's total giving?' Captures gift date, amount, currency, gift type discriminator (cash, check, wire, in-kind, stock, crypto, matching, tribute, refund/adjustment, recurring), fund designation, campaign and appeal attribution, gift source (online, direct mail, event, major gift officer), payment method, batch reference, anonymous flag, restricted vs. unrestricted designation, and GL posting reference. For matching gifts: match ratio, matching employer/corporation, match request date, match approval status, match payment received date, maximum match amount. For tribute gifts: tribute type (in-memoriam, in-honor-of), honoree name, honoree relationship, notification recipient, notification sent flag. For refunds/adjustments: original gift reference, refund date, refund amount, refund reason, refund method, GL reversal reference. For acknowledgements: acknowledgement type, acknowledgement date, receipt number, delivery method, acknowledgement status, IRS-compliant language flag, goods-or-services disclosure. Core financial transaction for donor revenue recognition per FASB ASC 958 and IRS 501(c)(3) substantiation requirements.

products.name: pledge
products.description: Tracks multi-installment giving commitments, pledge agreements, and their individual installment schedules from donors, managed in Raisers Edge NXT and Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud. Captures pledge date, total pledge amount, installment schedule (monthly, quarterly, annual), number of installments, pledge balance outstanding, pledge status (active, fulfilled, lapsed, written-off), fund designation, campaign, appeal, reminder schedule, and write-off reason. Includes installment-level detail: individual due dates, scheduled amounts, actual payment dates, amounts paid, installment status (scheduled, paid, overdue, skipped, waived), payment method, and linked gift reference upon payment. Enables granular pledge fulfillment tracking, overdue installment identification, automated reminder generation, and BvA (Budget vs. Actual) reconciliation for pledged revenue. Distinct from gift — a pledge is a commitment to give, not a completed transaction.

attributes.name: realization_date

attributes.name: realized_value

attributes.name: recognition_preference

attributes.name: record_updated_by

attributes.name: valuation_date

products.name: segment
products.description: Donor segmentation master records and constituent-to-segment membership assignments used for targeted fundraising, stewardship, and communication strategies. Captures segment definition (name, type, criteria, owner, creation date, status) and constituent membership records including assignment date, assigned-by staff member, assignment source (manual, automated RFM scoring, wealth screening import), expiry date, is_active flag, and segment transition history. Segment types include giving level (major, mid-level, annual), recency-frequency-monetary (RFM) tier, donor type, geographic, programmatic interest, acquisition channel, and lifecycle stage. Enables LYBUNT (Last Year But Unfortunately Not This Year), SYBUNT, and RFM-based segmentation for direct mail, email, and major gift cultivation strategies. Supports point-in-time segment membership queries and longitudinal donor behavior analysis.

attributes.references: Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) ASC 958; Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) for Nonprofits

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the soft credit record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Framework; Audit Trail Standards

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the soft credit amount. Ensures accurate multi-currency tracking and reporting for international donor relationships.

attributes.name: fiscal_year
attributes.description: Fiscal year in which the soft credit is recorded for financial and fundraising reporting purposes. Format typically YYYY or FY-YYYY depending on organizational convention.
attributes.references: Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) ASC 958; Internal Fiscal Calendar

attributes.name: is_anonymous
attributes.description: Indicates whether the soft credit should be treated as anonymous in public recognition and reporting. True if anonymous, False if public recognition is permitted. Respects donor privacy preferences.
attributes.references: Donor Privacy Best Practices; General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) Article 6

attributes.name: lifetime_value_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this soft credit amount should be included in the credited constituent's lifetime giving value calculation. True if included in lifetime value, False if excluded. Used to ensure accurate donor lifetime value metrics.
attributes.references: Donor Analytics Best Practices; Constituent Relationship Management (CRM) Standards

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the soft credit record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Framework; Audit Trail Standards

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional context, special instructions, or explanatory information about the soft credit attribution. Used by fundraising staff to document attribution rationale or special circumstances.

attributes.name: recognition_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this soft credit counts toward donor recognition levels, giving societies, or cumulative giving milestones. True if eligible for recognition programs, False if excluded.
attributes.references: Donor Recognition Best Practices; Raisers Edge NXT Recognition Framework

attributes.name: soft_credit_date
attributes.description: Date when the soft credit was recorded or attributed. Typically matches the gift date but may differ if soft credit is applied retroactively or during gift processing workflows.
attributes.references: Raisers Edge NXT Gift Processing; Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud Gift Attribution

attributes.name: soft_credit_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the soft credit record. Active indicates the credit is valid and counted in reports. Inactive indicates the credit has been deactivated. Reversed indicates the credit was removed due to gift refund or correction. Pending indicates the credit is awaiting approval or verification.
attributes.references: Internal Data Management Standard; Raisers Edge NXT Status Framework

attributes.name: soft_credit_type
attributes.description: Classification of the soft credit attribution. Defines the relationship or role of the credited constituent to the gift. Common types include household member (spouse/partner sharing credit), solicitor credit (fundraiser who secured the gift), matching gift credit (employer matching program), tribute notification recipient (honoree or memorial notification), gift officer (staff member managing the relationship), and volunteer solicitor (board member or volunteer who influenced the gift).
attributes.references: Raisers Edge NXT Soft Credit Types; Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud Attribution Framework

attributes.name: solicitor_relationship
attributes.description: Describes the relationship of the credited constituent to the organization or primary donor. Used to segment soft credit attribution by relationship type for performance analysis and stewardship planning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: staff|board_member|volunteer|peer|family|advisor|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Donor Stewardship Best Practices; Raisers Edge NXT Relationship Framework

attributes.name: source_record_reference
attributes.description: Unique identifier of the soft credit record in the source system. Enables traceability back to the originating system for reconciliation and audit purposes.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Framework; Data Lineage Standards

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this soft credit record originated. Used for data lineage tracking and system integration auditing.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Framework; Data Lineage Standards

attributes.name: split_from_soft_credit_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on soft_credit (split_from_soft_credit_id)

products.name: appeal_targeting
products.description: This association product represents the targeting relationship between fundraising appeals and donor segments. It captures the operational execution of multi-segment direct marketing campaigns where a single appeal is deployed to multiple constituent segments with segment-specific performance tracking. Each record links one appeal to one donor segment with attributes that measure the effectiveness of that specific appeal-segment combination including pieces sent, response metrics, revenue attribution, and ROI analysis.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit fundraising operations, appeals routinely target multiple donor segments simultaneously with segment-specific execution parameters (different ask amounts for major vs. annual donors, different creative variants for A/B testing, wave-based deployment schedules). Each appeal-segment combination generates its own performance metrics (pieces sent, response rate, revenue, ROI) that fundraisers actively analyze to optimize future targeting decisions. This is not a theoretical correlation but an operational business process where development teams create targeting plans, execute multi-segment campaigns, and measure segment-level results.

attributes.name: appeal_targeting_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this appeal-segment targeting record. Primary key.

attributes.name: appeal_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the fundraising appeal being deployed to this segment

attributes.name: donor_segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key to the donor_segment product

attributes.name: segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the donor segment being targeted by this appeal

attributes.name: staff_member_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the staff member who created this targeting assignment.

attributes.name: average_gift_amount
attributes.description: Average gift size for responses from this segment to this appeal, calculated as total_revenue_amount / response_count. Used to compare segment giving capacity.

attributes.name: cost_allocated
attributes.description: Portion of the total appeal cost allocated to this segment based on pieces sent or other cost allocation methodology. Enables segment-level ROI calculation.

attributes.name: cost_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the allocated cost amount.

attributes.name: created_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this appeal-segment targeting record was created in the system.

attributes.name: deployment_date
attributes.description: Date when the appeal was deployed to this specific segment. May differ from overall appeal mailing_date if segments are deployed in waves.

attributes.name: last_updated_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when performance metrics for this appeal-segment combination were last updated.

attributes.name: pieces_sent
attributes.description: Number of solicitation pieces (letters, emails, calls) sent specifically to constituents in this segment for this appeal. This is segment-specific volume tracking.

attributes.name: response_count
attributes.description: Number of constituents from this segment who responded to this appeal with a gift or pledge. Enables segment-level response analysis.

attributes.name: response_rate_percent
attributes.description: Response rate percentage for this specific appeal-segment combination, calculated as (response_count / pieces_sent) * 100. Critical metric for segment performance evaluation.

attributes.name: revenue_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the segment revenue amount (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: roi_ratio
attributes.description: Return on investment ratio for this appeal-segment combination, calculated as total_revenue_amount / cost_allocated. Critical metric for optimizing future segment targeting decisions.

attributes.name: segment_ask_amount
attributes.description: Suggested gift amount presented to constituents in this segment, which may differ from the general appeal ask_amount based on segment giving capacity (e.g., major donors receive higher asks).

attributes.name: target_segment
attributes.description: Description of the constituent segment targeted by this appeal (e.g., lapsed donors 12-24 months, major gift prospects $10K+, monthly sustainers). [Moved from appeal: The target_segment STRING attribute in appeal is a text description that cannot capture the reality of multi-segment targeting. When an appeal targets multiple segments (e.g., 'Major Donors', 'LYBUNT Q1', 'Mid-Level Annual'), this single STRING field would require concatenation or comma-separated values, making it impossible to query segment-specific performance. This attribute should be removed from appeal as the relationship is now properly modeled through the appeal_targeting association.]

attributes.name: test_variant
attributes.description: Identifier for A/B test variant or creative package version used for this segment (e.g., 'Control', 'Variant_A', 'High_Ask'). Enables multivariate testing across segments.

attributes.name: total_revenue_amount
attributes.description: Total gross revenue generated by gifts and pledges from this segment in response to this appeal. Enables segment-level revenue attribution and ROI calculation.

products.name: event_registration
products.description: This association product represents the registration and attendance relationship between constituents and fundraising events. It captures the complete lifecycle of constituent participation in donor cultivation and fundraising activities, from initial registration through post-event follow-up. Each record links one constituent to one fundraising event with transactional attributes including registration details, ticketing information, seating assignments, payment tracking, attendance confirmation, and stewardship workflow status. This is a core operational entity managed actively by development and events staff for capacity planning, revenue tracking, donor engagement measurement, and post-event cultivation workflows.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit fundraising operations, constituents register for and attend multiple fundraising events over their donor lifecycle (galas, golf tournaments, cultivation dinners), and each event hosts multiple constituent attendees. Event registration is an actively managed operational process with its own lifecycle: registration → payment → seating assignment → check-in → post-event follow-up. This is distinct from gift processing—not all attendees make gifts, and registration data (ticket type, table assignment, dietary restrictions, attendance confirmation) is managed separately from donation transactions.

attributes.name: event_registration_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this event registration record. Primary key.

attributes.name: constituent_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the constituent who registered for or attended the fundraising event

attributes.name: fundraising_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the fundraising event for which the constituent registered

attributes.name: attendance_status
attributes.description: The current status of the constituent's attendance (registered, confirmed, checked_in, no_show, cancelled). Tracks the registration lifecycle from initial signup through event day check-in. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: auction_paddle_number
attributes.description: The paddle or bidder number assigned to the constituent for auction participation at the event. Links to auction transaction tracking. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: check_in_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when the constituent checked in at the event. Used to confirm actual attendance and trigger post-event stewardship workflows.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this registration record was created in the system.

attributes.name: dietary_restrictions
attributes.description: Any dietary restrictions or meal preferences specified by the constituent during registration (vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, allergies). Used for catering planning. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: guest_count
attributes.description: The number of guests included in this registration (e.g., table sponsorships may include multiple seats). Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this registration record was last updated.

attributes.name: payment_method
attributes.description: The method of payment used for the registration (credit card, check, cash, wire transfer, complimentary). Supports reconciliation and revenue tracking.

attributes.name: payment_status
attributes.description: The current payment status for this registration (paid, pending, refunded, waived). Tracks financial completion of the registration.

attributes.name: post_event_follow_up_status
attributes.description: The status of post-event stewardship and cultivation follow-up activities for this constituent (pending, thank_you_sent, survey_sent, completed). Tracks donor engagement workflow completion.

attributes.name: registration_date
attributes.description: The date on which the constituent registered for the fundraising event. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: registration_source
attributes.description: The channel through which the constituent registered for the event (online, phone, mail, in-person, staff entry). Used for marketing effectiveness analysis.

attributes.name: registration_type
attributes.description: The type of registration or participation role for this constituent at the event (attendee, table sponsor, individual sponsor, volunteer). Determines engagement level and stewardship approach.

attributes.name: special_requests
attributes.description: Any special requests or accommodations requested by the constituent (accessibility needs, seating preferences, VIP treatment). Used for event logistics and donor stewardship.

attributes.name: table_number
attributes.description: The table number or seating assignment for the constituent at the event. Used for seating logistics and VIP placement. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data (table_assignment/table_number).

attributes.name: ticket_price_paid
attributes.description: The actual amount paid by the constituent for their ticket or registration. May differ from standard ticket price due to discounts, early bird pricing, or sponsorship levels. Corresponds to amount_paid in detection phase data.

attributes.name: ticket_type
attributes.description: The specific ticket tier or type purchased by the constituent (e.g., general admission, VIP, early bird). Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

products.name: participation
products.description: This association product represents the participation event between constituent and campaign. It captures every instance of constituent engagement with a fundraising campaign, including solicitation attempts, responses, gifts, pledges, volunteer activities, and advocacy actions. Each record links one constituent to one campaign with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific engagement instance.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit fundraising operations, constituents participate in multiple campaigns over time (annual fund, emergency appeals, capital campaigns, etc.), and each campaign engages multiple constituents through various solicitation channels. Campaign participation is a recognized business concept that fundraising teams actively manage, track, and analyze. The relationship carries rich operational data including participation type, solicitation channel, response outcomes, gift/pledge amounts, and volunteer hours that belong to neither the constituent nor the campaign alone but to each specific engagement instance.

attributes.name: participation_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this participation record. Primary key.

attributes.name: campaign_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the campaign in which the constituent participated

attributes.name: constituent_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the constituent who participated in the campaign

attributes.name: staff_member_id
attributes.description: Reference to the staff member who solicited or engaged this constituent for this campaign. Enables tracking of fundraiser effectiveness.

attributes.name: acknowledgment_sent_date
attributes.description: The date when acknowledgment communication was sent to the constituent for this participation. Null if not yet sent.

attributes.name: acknowledgment_sent_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a thank-you or acknowledgment communication was sent to the constituent for this participation. Used for stewardship tracking.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this participation record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: gift_amount
attributes.description: The monetary amount contributed by the constituent to this campaign in this participation instance. Null if participation type is not gift. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: participation_date
attributes.description: The date when this participation event occurred. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: participation_type
attributes.description: The type of participation or engagement activity. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data. Values include solicitation (outreach attempt), gift (monetary contribution), pledge (commitment to give), volunteer (time contribution), advocacy (campaign promotion), event_attendance (campaign event participation), non_response (solicited but did not respond).

attributes.name: pledge_amount
attributes.description: The monetary amount pledged by the constituent to this campaign in this participation instance. Null if participation type is not pledge. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: response_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the constituent responded to the campaign solicitation. True = responded (gift, pledge, volunteer, etc.); False = solicited but no response. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: solicitation_channel
attributes.description: The communication channel through which the constituent was solicited or engaged for this campaign. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this participation record was last modified.

attributes.name: volunteer_hours
attributes.description: The number of hours the constituent volunteered for this campaign in this participation instance. Null if participation type is not volunteer. Explicitly identified in detection phase relationship data.

products.name: segment_membership
products.description: This association product represents the membership relationship between constituents and donor segments. It captures the assignment of constituents to fundraising and stewardship segments for targeted communication, cultivation, and reporting. Each record links one constituent to one donor segment with temporal, attribution, and scoring attributes that exist only in the context of this specific membership assignment.. Existence Justification: Constituent segmentation is a core operational fundraising process where nonprofits actively manage multi-dimensional segment assignments. Constituents simultaneously belong to multiple segments (e.g., a major donor can be in 'Major Donors 2024', 'LYBUNT Q1', 'East Coast Region', and 'Health Program Interest' at the same time), and each segment contains many constituents. The business manages segment membership as a distinct lifecycle with assignment rules, temporal tracking, scoring attribution, and transition history for targeted cultivation, stewardship, and campaign execution.

attributes.name: segment_membership_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this segment membership record. Primary key.

attributes.name: constituent_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the constituent who is a member of this donor segment

attributes.name: donor_segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key to donor_segment. Part of the many-to-many relationship.

attributes.name: segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the donor segment to which the constituent is assigned

attributes.name: staff_member_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the staff member (fundraiser, development officer, or data analyst) who manually assigned this constituent to the segment. Null for automated assignments. Referenced in Product B description as assignment attribution.

attributes.name: assignment_method
attributes.description: Method by which the constituent was assigned to this segment (manual, automated RFM scoring, wealth screening import, campaign response, lifecycle trigger, data import). Explicitly identified in detection reasoning as relationship data.

attributes.name: assignment_source
attributes.description: Source system or process that created this membership record (e.g., 'Salesforce NPSP', 'Raiser's Edge NXT', 'RFM Batch Job', 'Manual Entry'). Referenced in Product B description.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this segment membership record was created in the system.

attributes.name: is_active
attributes.description: Indicates whether this segment membership is currently active. Explicitly identified in detection reasoning as relationship data.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this segment membership record was last updated.

attributes.name: membership_end_date
attributes.description: Date when the constituent membership in this segment ended or expired. Null for active memberships. Explicitly identified in detection reasoning as relationship data.

attributes.name: membership_start_date
attributes.description: Date when the constituent was assigned to this donor segment. Explicitly identified in detection reasoning as relationship data.

attributes.name: score_at_assignment
attributes.description: RFM score, wealth rating, or other quantitative score that qualified the constituent for this segment at the time of assignment. Explicitly identified in detection reasoning as relationship data.

attributes.name: segment_assignment_reason
attributes.description: Business rationale or rule that triggered this segment assignment (e.g., 'Total giving >$10K in FY2024', 'LYBUNT - gave $5K in 2023, $0 in 2024', 'Wealth screening capacity $100K+'). Explicitly identified in detection reasoning as relationship data.

products.name: indicator_funding
products.description: This association product represents the funding relationship between a constituent (donor/funder) and a specific MEL indicator. It captures donor-specific funding allocations, restrictions, targets, and reporting requirements for individual indicators across programs and grants. Each record links one constituent to one indicator with funding terms, amounts, timeframes, and performance targets that exist only in the context of this donor-indicator funding relationship. Essential for donor-specific impact reporting, compliance with funder restrictions, and tracking indicator-level funding sources.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit operations, donors (bilateral agencies like USAID/DFID, multilateral organizations, foundations) fund specific MEL indicators across multiple programs and grants, and each indicator receives funding from multiple donor sources. The business actively manages these donor-indicator funding relationships with specific funding amounts, timeframes, restrictions (unrestricted vs. earmarked), donor-specific targets, and reporting frequencies that differ by donor. This is a recognized operational concept called 'Donor Indicator Funding' or 'Indicator-Level Funding Allocation' that program managers and MEL officers actively create, track, and report on for donor compliance and impact reporting.

attributes.name: indicator_funding_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this donor-indicator funding relationship record. Primary key.

attributes.name: constituent_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the constituent (donor/funder) providing funding for this indicator

attributes.name: indicator_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the MEL indicator being funded by this constituent

attributes.name: created_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this donor-indicator funding relationship was created in the system.

attributes.name: donor_target_value
attributes.description: The donor-specific target value for this indicator, which may differ from the indicator's overall target. Represents what this specific donor expects to achieve with their funding contribution.

attributes.name: funding_amount
attributes.description: The monetary amount allocated by this donor specifically for this indicator. Currency should align with constituent's preferred currency or grant currency.

attributes.name: funding_end_date
attributes.description: The date when donor funding for this indicator expires or the funding period ends.

attributes.name: funding_start_date
attributes.description: The date when donor funding for this indicator becomes active and eligible for expenditure.

attributes.name: grant_reference_number
attributes.description: The donor's grant or award reference number under which this indicator funding is provided. Links to the broader grant agreement.

attributes.name: indicator_funding_status
attributes.description: Current status of this donor-indicator funding relationship. Active = currently funded; Pending = approved but not yet active; Completed = funding period ended; Suspended = temporarily paused; Cancelled = funding withdrawn.

attributes.name: modified_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this donor-indicator funding relationship was last modified.

attributes.name: reporting_frequency
attributes.description: How often this donor requires progress reporting specifically for this indicator. May differ from the indicator's standard reporting frequency due to donor-specific requirements.

attributes.name: restriction_type
attributes.description: The type of restriction the donor has placed on this indicator funding. Unrestricted = no restrictions; Restricted = tied to specific activities/geographies; Temporarily Restricted = time-bound restrictions; Permanently Restricted = endowment-style restrictions; Earmarked = donor-specified use.

products.name: event_volunteer_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the operational assignment of volunteers to fundraising events. It captures the specific role, shift timing, and attendance tracking for each volunteer serving at each event. Each record links one fundraising event to one volunteer with attributes that exist only in the context of this assignment relationship, enabling event staffing management, volunteer coordination, and post-event reporting.. Existence Justification: Fundraising events require multiple volunteers serving in different operational roles (registration, setup, catering, cleanup), and volunteers serve at multiple events throughout the year. The nonprofit actively manages event volunteer assignments as a distinct operational process, coordinating staffing needs, assigning specific roles and shifts, tracking attendance via check-in/check-out, and recording hours worked for each volunteer at each event. This is not a derived correlation but an operational entity that event managers create, update, and monitor.

attributes.name: event_volunteer_assignment_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the event volunteer assignment record. Primary key.

attributes.name: fundraising_event_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Event Volunteer Assignment - Fundraising Event Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the fundraising event where the volunteer is assigned to serve

attributes.name: volunteer_id

attributes.name: assignment_date

attributes.name: assignment_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes specific to this volunteer assignment, such as special instructions, accommodation needs, or post-event feedback.

attributes.name: assignment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the volunteer assignment (confirmed, pending, cancelled, completed). Tracks the state of this specific assignment.

attributes.name: check_in_status
attributes.description: Current attendance status of the volunteer for this event assignment (not arrived, checked in, checked out, no show). Tracks actual attendance vs. scheduled assignment.

attributes.name: check_in_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the volunteer checked in at the event venue or virtual platform. Null if not yet checked in.

attributes.name: check_out_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the volunteer checked out after completing their shift. Null if not yet checked out.

attributes.name: hours_worked
attributes.description: The actual number of hours the volunteer worked at this event, calculated from check-in/check-out or manually recorded. Used for volunteer engagement tracking and reporting.

attributes.name: role_assignment
attributes.description: The specific role or function assigned to the volunteer for this event (e.g., registration desk, setup crew, catering support, cleanup, greeter, auction support). This attribute exists only in the context of the assignment.

attributes.name: shift_end_time
attributes.description: The scheduled end date and time for the volunteer's shift at this event. Specific to this volunteer-event assignment.

attributes.name: shift_start_time
attributes.description: The scheduled start date and time for the volunteer's shift at this event. Specific to this volunteer-event assignment.

domains.name: field

products.name: assessment
